articles.headline: OFAC Designates Individuals and Entities in Latest Counter Terrorism Action
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new designations today as part of its ongoing counter-terrorism efforts. This action targets individuals and entities found to be involved in supporting terrorist activities.
Further details regarding the specific individuals and entities designated, and the nature of their support for terrorism, are expected to be released by OFAC.
These designations aim to disrupt financial networks and limit the ability of terrorist organizations to operate globally.

articles.headline: OFAC Sanctions Guatemalan Drug Trafficking Organizations Linked to Mexican Cartels
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has imposed sanctions on several Guatemalan drug trafficking organizations, including 'LOS LORENZANAS,' 'LOS MENDOZA DRUG TRAFFICKING ORGANIZATION,' and 'LOS HUISTAS DRUG TRAFFICKING ORGANIZATION.' These groups are accused of supporting Mexican narco-terrorist cartels, specifically the Sinaloa Cartel and Cartel de Jalisco Nueva Generación.

The designations were made under counter-narcotics and counter-terrorism authorities, including Executive Orders 13224 and 14059. OFAC stated that these organizations play a crucial role in moving illicit drugs and providing logistical and financial support to the Mexican cartels.
This action is part of a broader U.S. strategy to disrupt transnational criminal organizations and their financial networks that pose a threat to international security.
articles.source: U.S. Treasury OFAC / ABA Banking Journal

articles.headline: OFAC Updates Designation for Iran-Linked Volta Shipping Services
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has issued an update to an existing Iran-related designation, specifically for Volta Shipping Services LLC. The update changes the listed alias for the UAE-based company from Volta Shipping Services FZCO to Volta Container Line FZCO.

Volta Shipping Services LLC remains designated under Executive Order 13902 and continues to be subject to secondary sanctions risk. This action is part of OFAC's ongoing efforts to maintain the accuracy and effectiveness of its sanctions lists.
The company is linked to Mohammad Hossein Shamkhani, and the update clarifies its identity for compliance purposes.
articles.source: U.S. Treasury OFAC / ABA Banking Journal

articles.headline: OFAC Sanctions Eight Canada-Based Money Services Businesses for Iran Transactions
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has sanctioned eight Canada-based money services businesses (MSBs) for facilitating transactions involving Iran. This action, part of 'Operation Economic Outcast,' targets international financial channels used by Iran to evade sanctions.

These MSBs are accused of converting Iranian currency into digital assets and conducting transactions with sanctioned Iranian exchanges and digital asset addresses linked to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC).
The designations were coordinated with FinCEN and Canada's FINTRAC and were taken under Executive Order 13902, aiming to disrupt Iran's ability to access the global financial system.
articles.source: U.S. Treasury OFAC / ABA Banking Journal

articles.headline: OFAC Designates Entities for Cyber-related and Transnational Criminal Activities; Issues Cuba Designations and Determination
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has announced new designations targeting entities involved in cyber-related activities and transnational criminal organizations. This action underscores the U.S. government's commitment to combating illicit activities that threaten national security and financial stability.

In a separate but related move, OFAC also issued new designations related to Cuba, alongside the publication of a Cuba-related determination. These actions reflect ongoing efforts to address various threats through targeted sanctions.
Further details on the specific entities and individuals designated under these authorities are expected to be provided by OFAC.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues New Iran-related Designations, Updates Listings, and Amends Venezuela GL
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has announced new Iran-related designations and provided updates to certain existing Iran-related listings. These actions are part of the U.S. Treasury's ongoing efforts to counter Iranian malign activities.

In conjunction with these designations, OFAC also published an Iran-related alert to provide guidance to the public. Additionally, an amended Venezuela-related General License and a new Frequently Asked Question were issued, indicating adjustments to sanctions policy concerning Venezuela.
These measures aim to enhance the effectiveness of U.S. sanctions programs and address evolving threats in both Iran and Venezuela.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues Amended Iran-related General License for Wind Down of International Development Bank for Investment and Finance
body: The Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has issued Iran General License FF-1, titled 'Authorizing the Wind Down of Transactions Involving International Development Bank for Investment and Finance.'
This amended general license permits a wind-down period for transactions related to the specified entity, providing clarity and a limited timeframe for businesses to cease operations or dealings.
The issuance of such a license typically indicates a strategic adjustment in sanctions enforcement, allowing for an orderly disengagement from the designated entity.
articles.source: U.S. Treasury OFAC / Bank Data Insights / GovDelivery

articles.region: North Korea / Democratic Republic of the Congo
articles.headline: OFAC Sanctions North Korea IT Worker Facilitators and Rwandan Ministry of Defence
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has announced new designations targeting facilitators of North Korean IT worker fraud and entities supporting destabilizing activities in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC).

Among the North Korea-related designations are individuals and entities, including 'FIRST FINANCIAL AND TECHNICAL DEVELOPMENT CENTER' in North Korea and Vladivostok, Russia, and individuals like Ilya Aleksandrovich Boykov, Han Yu Song, and Ri Thae Chol, all linked to facilitating DPRK IT worker fraud.
Additionally, OFAC sanctioned the Rwandan Ministry of Defence and a financial institution for their support of the M23 rebel group, which is contributing to instability in the eastern DRC.

articles.headline: Extreme Networks Settles with OFAC for $1.5 Million Over Russia Sanctions Violations
body: Extreme Networks, Inc., a North Carolina-based cloud networking solutions provider, has reached a settlement with the U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) for $1,529,685. The settlement resolves nine apparent violations of the Ukraine-/Russia-Related Sanctions Regulations.

Between September 2018 and March 2022, Extreme Networks exported networking equipment and related services to Joint Stock Company (JSC) Moskovskiy Mashinostroitelniy Zavod Avangard (MMZA), a Russian defense manufacturer. MMZA was blocked by operation of law due to being majority-owned by the designated JSC Concern Almaz Antey.

OFAC determined that the violations were voluntarily self-disclosed and egregious. A parallel non-prosecution agreement was also reached with the Department of Justice, with Extreme Networks agreeing to pay nearly $1 million in criminal penalties, a portion of which will be credited against the OFAC settlement.
articles.source: U.S. Treasury OFAC / Corruption, Crime & Compliance / Zyphe

articles.headline: OFAC Amends FAQs on Blocking, Rejecting Transactions, and Filing Reports
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has amended several Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) as part of its ongoing review of published guidance. The updates specifically address topics related to blocking and rejecting transactions, as well as filing reports with OFAC.

Eleven FAQs (numbers 10, 32, 33, 34, 35, 36, 41, 42, 49, 50, and 53) have been revised to ensure that information remains current and provides clearer explanations for financial institutions and other entities.

The amendments clarify procedures for blocking accounts, handling interest on blocked funds, deducting service charges, and distinguishing between transactions that require blocking versus rejection. They also provide updated guidance on reporting blocked property and rejected transactions to OFAC.
articles.source: U.S. Treasury OFAC / Sanctions Law Center / KPMG

articles.headline: Extreme Networks, Inc. Pays $1,529,685 for Russia Sanctions Violations
body: Extreme Networks, Inc., a North Carolina-based cloud networking solutions provider, has paid $1,529,685 to settle apparent violations of the Ukraine-/Russia-Related Sanctions Regulations. The violations involved nine instances of exporting networking equipment and services to a Russian defense manufacturer, JSC Moskovskiy Mashinostroitelniy Zavod Avangard (MMZA), which was blocked by operation of law.

The settlement amount reflects OFAC's determination that the apparent violations were voluntarily self-disclosed and egregious. A parallel non-prosecution agreement with the Department of Justice also resulted in criminal penalties, with a portion credited against the OFAC settlement.

The case highlights the importance of thorough due diligence, especially in acquisitions, as MMZA's blocked status was due to its majority ownership by the designated JSC Concern Almaz Antey, a fact that Extreme Networks' compliance team initially missed.

articles.headline: UK Inflation Rises to 3.6% in October Amid Soaring Fuel Prices and Iran War Fallout
body: The UK's inflation rate, as measured by the Consumer Prices Index (CPI), increased to 3.6% in October 2026, up from 3.5% in September. This rise marks the highest level in a year and is primarily attributed to record-high petrol and diesel prices.

The Office for National Statistics (ONS) reported that fuel prices were the major contributor, with annual costs of raw materials and goods leaving factories also climbing due to rising energy and crude oil prices, exacerbated by the ongoing conflict in the Middle East.

Households are bracing for further increases, with energy bills in Great Britain forecast to rise by 26% from January 2027, pushing the average annual bill to £2,166. This sustained inflationary pressure is expected to prompt the Bank of England to consider further interest rate hikes.
articles.source: The Guardian / Office for National Statistics / Forbes

articles.headline: Euro Area Annual Inflation Climbs to 4.0% in October
body: The annual inflation rate in the euro area reached 4.0% in October 2026, an increase from 3.8% in September. This figure, released by Eurostat, indicates a continued upward trend in consumer prices across the European Union.
Energy prices were the largest contributor to the annual euro area inflation rate, followed by services, non-energy industrial goods, and food, alcohol & tobacco.
Compared with September, annual inflation fell in nine Member States, remained stable in two, and rose in sixteen, highlighting varied inflationary pressures across the region.

articles.headline: BIS Imposes New Export Controls on Remote Access to Advanced AI Chips
body: The U.S. Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) has released an interim final rule imposing new export licensing requirements on remote access to and exports of advanced-node integrated circuits (AI chips). The rule, effective upon publication in the Federal Register on November 19, 2026, aims to prevent foreign actors from circumventing existing restrictions on sensitive American technology.

The new regulations require a license to export, reexport, or transfer (in-country) AI chips if the exporter has 'knowledge' that the item is destined for a data center providing access to more than 12 million 'aggregate TPP' (total processing performance) to companies headquartered in, or whose ultimate parent is headquartered in, Macau or a Country Group D:5 destination (including China, Belarus, and Russia).

Additionally, the rule introduces new license requirements for transfers of advanced AI semiconductors to or within Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Brazil, which are viewed as diversion risks. It also formally rescinds most of the Biden-era AI Diffusion Rule.
articles.source: Fenwick / Reed Smith LLP / Sidley Austin LLP / Bureau of Industry and Security

articles.headline: Streamlining Export Controls for Drone Exports
body: The Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is easing export controls on certain Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs or drones) and related parts, components, accessories, attachments, technology, and software under the Export Administration Regulations (EAR). Specifically, this rule: eliminates wind gust tolerance as a parameter for determining UAV controls under the EAR; increases the threshold for national security controls on certain UAVs from an endurance of 30 minutes to an endurance of 3 hours; makes conforming changes to remove national security controls on software and technology associated with UAVs with an endurance less than 3 hours; maintains military end-use and end-user controls on those lower endurance drones and associated software and technology; clarifies Commerce Control List (CCL) controls for certain UAVs specially designed for military use; and removes national security controls on certain specially designed parts, components, accessories, and attachments for such UAVs as they do not provide any significant military or intelligence capabilities.

body: The decision comes after California banned Waymo's driverless vehicles from operating on the state's highways following a series of traffic incidents.

articles.headline: Rubio says US not 'under systemic attack' after series of tech outages
body: Secretary of State Marco Rubio said there was "zero evidence" supporting theories online that recent disruptions affecting Microsoft, banks and flights are connected.

articles.headline: Irishman charged with destroying US military aircraft with axe
body: The $60m (£45m) plane was destroyed in an hours-long raid by an anti-war protester, according to the FBI.

articles.headline: US loses measles elimination status after 26 years amid record case numbers
body: States have reported over 5,400 cases and 10 measles-related deaths for the first time since the early 1990s.

articles.headline: American soldier arrested by UK police on suspicion of spying taken into US military custody
body: The Metropolitan Police say he has been taken into custody by the US Military over suspected national security and espionage allegations.

articles.headline: Palestinian woman, 72, shot dead by Israeli settlers in West Bank, health ministry says
body: Palestinians say there was an attack by settlers in al-Duyuk al-Tahta, while the Israeli military says the settlers fired after being attacked.

articles.headline: William and Kate celebrate Earthshot Prize winners in Mumbai
body: The Prince and Princess of Wales were joined by sporting and acting stars for the annual environmental awards ceremony.

articles.headline: New video shows explosions moments before part of Crimea Bridge collapses
body: BBC Verify analyses footage showing the final moments before part of the bridge fell and videos showing the scale of destruction.
